ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Trace mitral regurgitation, physiological. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 152 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 4/mm3. Protein 78 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 62 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.71). Gram stain: no organisms. CMV PCR and HSV PCR not detected. Cultures: no growth. Elevated protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation). Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: No T2 signal abnormality; no lesion at T4
Mild diffuse enhancement of the spinal nerve roots after gadolinium
Mild C5-C6 degenerative changes without cord compression

output.impression: 1. No signal abnormality in the cervical or thoracic spinal cord; no lesion at the T4 level or elsewhere. 2. Mild diffuse nerve root enhancement throughout the imaged spine, consistent with an inflammatory polyradiculopathy. 3. Mild C5-C6 degenerative changes without cord compression.
Bedside respiratory function 6 h after admission: FVC 2.2 L (55% predicted; 29 mL/kg at 76 kg) L. MIP -26 cmH2O L. MEP 42 cmH2O L. Change: FVC 2.4 L to 2.2 L over 6 h (8% fall). Cough weak.

quantitative_data.previous: FVC 2.4 L, MIP -30 cmH2O 6 h earlier

events.event: Blood pressure 178/104 mmHg, settled to 146/90 mmHg within 40 minutes
Sinus bradycardia 48 bpm, self-limited, no pause

output.impression: 24-hour continuous telemetry. 1. Sinus tachycardia while awake (maximum 118 bpm) with a self-limited sinus bradycardia to 48 bpm overnight; no pauses. 2. Labile blood pressure, 122/78 to 178/104 mmHg.
output.rhythm_summary: Sinus tachycardia while awake with a self-limited nocturnal sinus bradycardia.

interactions: IVIg: no interaction with a current medication (none recorded).
output.proposed: IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days; no current medications (macrolide course completed)
warnings: Macrolides and fluoroquinolones prolong the QT interval; the risk is additive with a borderline QTc (458 ms) and autonomic involvement (relative caution).
IVIg: renal impairment and thrombosis are recognised risks; renal function is checked before infusion and hydration maintained (IVIg SmPC).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies show a demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy, which separates GBS with sensory ataxia from a sensory ganglionopathy (normal motor conduction) and from a cord lesion [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and, with a normal cell count and negative viral PCR, removes the viral meningoencephalitis the serology suggested [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No cord lesion at T4 or elsewhere; nerve root enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Contrast spine MRI to exclude a cord lesion behind the apparent T4 sensory level
action_criteria.rationale: A sensory level is a red flag for a spinal cord lesion; even though detailed testing found it patchy, imaging is needed to exclude it [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics and give the baseline before IVIg [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: He cannot stand, has facial and bulbar involvement and is still progressing; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level care and intubation planning [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus tachycardia to 118 bpm, a self-limited sinus bradycardia to 48 bpm and blood pressure 122/78 to 178/104 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus tachycardia 104 bpm with a borderline prolonged QTc (458 ms) and no conduction or ST-T abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No current interacting medicine; QT-prolonging antibiotics are a caution if one is needed again
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check before IVIg (no current medications; macrolide course completed)
action_criteria.rationale: The macrolide course is finished and he takes no medicines, so the check does not change the immediate plan.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on GBS with sensory ataxia
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not delay immunotherapy awaiting antibody or viral serology results.
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now: FVC 2.2 L (55% predicted, 29 mL/kg) falling from 2.4 L, MIP -26 cmH2O, weak cough and autonomic lability; repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 4-6 hours [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Plan elective intubation if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (1.5 L at 76 kg), MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, or bulbar function, cough or secretions worsen; intubate at once for respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia.

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 30 g/day at 76 kg) now: he cannot stand (GBS disability score 4) and is 10 days from onset; plasma exchange is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].

Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring for the autonomic lability (bradycardia to 48 bpm, blood pressure to 178/104 mmHg); avoid QT-prolonging drugs where an alternative exists (QTc 458 ms).
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (low-molecular-weight heparin) while he cannot walk [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for encephalopathy, long-tract signs or a brainstem syndrome. He is alert, the cranial neuropathies are lower motor neuron, and the CSF excludes meningoencephalitis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with sensory ataxia, after an upper respiratory infection

differential.diagnosis: Acute sensory-ataxic neuropathy (Sjögren-related or paraneoplastic ganglionopathy)
differential.key_features: Sensory ataxia fits, and he smokes, but limb weakness is marked and the NCS shows slowed motor conduction with absent F-waves; a ganglionopathy is purely sensory with normal motor studies.
Raised by the IgM serology, but he is alert, afebrile, without meningism, and the CSF has 4 cells/mm3 with negative CMV and HSV PCR.
The apparent T4 level was patchy on detailed testing, there are no upper motor neuron signs or sphincter symptoms, and the contrast spine MRI shows a normal cord with nerve root enhancement.
Ataxia and hyporeflexia are shared, but eye movements are full and limb weakness is prominent, which places the illness in GBS.
Cannot be excluded at 10 days; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it.
Subacute and chronic; does not produce limb weakness over 10 days with CSF albuminocytological dissociation and demyelinating conduction.

key_clinical_evidence: Sensory ataxia (vibration and joint position loss) with weakness, reduced reflexes, CSF protein 78 mg/dL with 4 cells/mm3 and a demyelinating sensorimotor NCS is GBS with sensory ataxia, not a ganglionopathy [EAN_PNS_2023].

Simultaneous low-titre IgM to CMV, EBV and HSV is typical of cross-reactivity or polyclonal activation, not of three active infections. The antecedent infection is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger.
A sensory level is a red flag for a cord lesion; here it was patchy on detailed testing and the contrast spine MRI shows a normal cord with nerve root enhancement [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019].
FVC 55% predicted and falling with MIP -26 cmH2O, a weak cough and autonomic lability meet ICU-level monitoring triggers [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Low-level IgM to CMV, EBV and HSV: simultaneous positivity is typical of cross-reactivity or polyclonal activation, not of three active infections, and does not change the diagnosis. He is alert and the CSF has 4 cells/mm3 with negative CMV and HSV PCR.
red_herrings.data_point: Low-titre IgM to CMV, EBV and HSV on serology sent before admission
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a viral meningoencephalitis or a specific viral trigger that must be treated first.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: On detailed testing the deficit is patchy without a sharp border, with no upper motor neuron signs or sphincter symptoms; the contrast spine MRI shows no cord lesion and nerve root enhancement, and the NCS is demyelinating.
red_herrings.data_point: Apparent T4 sensory level to temperature on initial screening
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a thoracic cord lesion rather than a polyradiculoneuropathy.

ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia, rate 104. Borderline prolonged QTc (458 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: CRP 18.2 mg/L and ESR 54 mm/hr (elevated). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

findings.finding: DML 7.2 ms (prolonged); CV 28 m/s (severely reduced); CMAP 2.4 mV (reduced)
DML 7.8 ms (prolonged); CV 26 m/s (severely reduced); CMAP 2.0 mV
R1 absent bilaterally; R2 delayed bilaterally
Tibialis anterior, vastus lateralis and deltoid bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal motor units; no fibrillation potentials

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies (peroneal 7.2 ms, tibial 7.8 ms, median 6.4 ms). 2. Severely reduced motor conduction velocities (peroneal 28 m/s, tibial 26 m/s, median 38 m/s) with reduced CMAPs. 3. Absent sural sensory responses; severely reduced median sensory amplitude (6 µV). 4. Absent F-waves in all nerves and absent H-reflexes. 5. Blink reflex: absent R1 and delayed R2 bilaterally, indicating facial nerve conduction slowing. 6. Reduced recruitment without denervation. Pattern consistent with a severe demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy with facial nerve involvement.

quantitative_data.pattern: Severe demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy with facial nerve involvement

metadata.difficulty_description: Apparent T4 sensory level simulating a cord lesion, triple viral IgM positivity suggesting viral encephalitis, and sensory ataxia: several concurrent red herrings
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry), 1 recommended mimic exclusion (contrast spine MRI), 2 red herrings (triple IgM serology, apparent T4 level).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden loss of temperature sensation followed by progressive leg unsteadiness and weakness, loss of taste and circumoral numbness, after an upper respiratory infection.

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. B. is a 41-year-old civil engineer presenting with a 10-day history of progressive neurological symptoms. He had an upper respiratory tract infection approximately 3 weeks ago, treated with a course of a macrolide antibiotic that he has completed; the infection resolved. On the day symptoms began, he noticed a sudden loss of hot and cold sensation while taking a shower. Over the following days he developed progressive unsteadiness and weakness in both legs, lost his sense of taste and noticed numbness around his mouth. By day 7 he could no longer stand without support. He has no bowel or bladder dysfunction and no back pain. He has no history of prior neurological symptoms. Viral serology sent by his primary care physician 3 days ago showed low-titre IgM antibodies to CMV, EBV and HSV.

neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose and heel-shin ataxic bilaterally, worse with eyes closed.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Eye movements full, no nystagmus. Pupils equal and reactive. Bilateral subtle lower motor neuron facial weakness. Reduced taste on the anterior tongue bilaterally. Mild dysarthria.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Cannot stand without support. Upper extremity 4/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Diminished bilateral patellar and Achilles (1+). Trace bilateral biceps. Plantars downgoing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced temperature sensation over the legs and trunk; an apparent level at T4 on initial screening is patchy without a sharp border on detailed testing. Vibration absent at the toes and ankles and reduced at the knees and fingers; joint position sense impaired at the toes and fingers. Pain and light touch relatively preserved distally. Circumoral numbness.
